overview: World War II was a global war fought from 1939 to 1945 between the Allies, which included Britain, the Soviet Union, the United States and China, and the Axis powers of Germany, Japan and Italy. The fighting spread across Europe, North Africa and the Pacific. During the war, Nazi Germany and its collaborators carried out the mass murder of European Jews. About six million European Jews were murdered in the Holocaust. The war in Europe ended with Germany's surrender in May 1945. Japan formally surrendered in September 1945. The war killed tens of millions of people.

keyMoments.title: Germany invades Poland
keyMoments.text: German troops crossed into **Poland** on 1 September 1939, days after Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union concluded the **Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact**. Two days later **Britain and France declared war on Germany**, turning a regional invasion into a European war. On 17 September the **Soviet Union invaded eastern Poland**. Germany and the Soviet Union divided the country after agreeing on spheres of influence in a secret protocol to the pact.

keyMoments.title: Barbarossa and Stalingrad
keyMoments.text: On 22 June 1941 Germany broke its pact with the Soviet Union and launched **Operation Barbarossa**. German forces advanced toward Moscow, where a Soviet counteroffensive pushed them back in December. Fighting reached **Stalingrad** on the Volga in 1942, and Soviet forces encircled the German **Sixth Army**. Its commander, Friedrich Paulus, entered Soviet captivity before the remaining German forces in the city surrendered on 2 February 1943.

keyMoments.title: Pearl Harbor brings in the United States
keyMoments.text: Japan, already at war with China since 1937, sent carrier aircraft against the **US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor** in Hawaii on the morning of 7 December 1941, sinking or damaging battleships and killing more than 2,400 Americans. The **United States declared war on Japan** the next day, and on 11 December **Germany and Italy declared war on the United States**, bringing the United States into the war against Germany and Italy as well. The US aircraft carriers escaped the attack. Six months later, US carrier aircraft fatally damaged four Japanese carriers at the **Battle of Midway**.

keyMoments.title: Surrender in Europe, atomic bombs in Asia
keyMoments.text: With Soviet troops in Berlin and Hitler dead by suicide, **Germany surrendered unconditionally**. Britain marked **Victory in Europe Day** on 8 May 1945. In August, the United States dropped atomic bombs on **Hiroshima** and **Nagasaki**, and the Soviet Union declared war on Japan and invaded Manchuria. Emperor Hirohito announced Japan's surrender in a radio broadcast on 15 August. Japan signed the formal surrender aboard **USS Missouri** in Tokyo Bay on 2 September 1945.

deepFacts.text: Before the war, Polish codebreakers including **Marian Rejewski** broke the German Enigma cipher. In July 1939, the Polish team shared its work with British and French counterparts near Warsaw. The disclosure gave British codebreakers a head start.

Japanese army lieutenant **Hiroo Onoda** continued to fight on Lubang Island in the Philippines after Japan surrendered, harming local residents. He laid down his arms in 1974 after a Japanese officer came to the island and gave him the order to stand down.

The **1956 Soviet–Japanese Joint Declaration** provided for an end to the state of war between the Soviet Union and Japan and for the restoration of diplomatic relations. It also committed both governments to further negotiations for a peace treaty.
